flawed_step: Lines 0014-0018: applying Master-theorem Case 1 to S(m)=S(m/2)+10 log m by claiming f(m)=10 log m = O(m^{log_2 1 - eps}) = O(m^{-0.5}), verified via lim 10 log m / m^{0.5} = 0, concluding S(m)=Theta(1).
counterexample: Take the recurrence exactly as the proof writes it, S(m) = S(m/2) + 10 log_2 m with base case S(1) = 0, and evaluate it at m = 2^k. Unrolling: S(2^k) = 10 * (log_2 2^k + log_2 2^{k-1} + ... + log_2 2^1) = 10 * (k + (k-1) + ... + 1) = 5k(k+1). Explicit values: S(1)=0, S(2)=10, S(4)=30, S(8)=60, S(16)=100, S(1024)=5*10*11=550, S(2^100)=5*100*101=50500. This sequence is unbounded, so S(m) is NOT Theta(1); in fact S(m) = Theta(log^2 m) (equivalently T(n) = Theta((log log n)^2)). The error is in the Case-1 hypothesis check: Case 1 with a=1, b=2 requires f(m) = O(m^{log_b a - eps}) = O(m^{-0.5}), i.e. 10 log m * m^{0.5} bounded, which fails since 10 log m * m^{0.5} -> infinity. The proof instead computed 10 log m / m^{0.5} -> 0, which is the reverse ratio and only shows f(m) = O(m^{+0.5}); concretely at m = 1024, f(m) = 10 log_2 1024 = 100 while m^{log_2 1} = 1, so f(m) dwarfs m^{log_b a} rather than being polynomially smaller than it. (Case 3 also fails, since f(m)=10 log m is not Omega(m^{eps}) for any eps>0; the correct tool is the Case-2 extension f(m)=Theta(m^0 log^k m) with k=1, giving Theta(log^2 m).)
reasoning_summary: The substitution m = log n and S(m) = T(2^m) giving S(m) = S(m/2) + 10 log m is fine. The failure is the Master-theorem application: with a=1, b=2 the watershed is m^{log_2 1} = m^0 = 1, and Case 1 demands the driving function be polynomially SMALLER than 1, i.e. f(m) = O(m^{-eps}). The proof's limit test 10 log m / m^{0.5} -> 0 checks the opposite comparison and would correspond to eps = -0.5, which is not permitted. Direct unrolling of the stated recurrence gives S(2^k) = 5k(k+1), an unbounded sequence (S(1024)=550, S(2^100)=50500), directly contradicting the claimed S = Theta(1). The true bound is S(m) = Theta(log^2 m), i.e. T(n) = Theta((log log n)^2). Line 0018 additionally conflates T with S. I stopped after confirming this counterexample.
